question: Should experimental Claw packages be allowed to claim, export, reconcile, and later remove globally named MCP server configuration under the agent-centric RFC model?
rationale: This determines ownership of executable configuration, persisted provenance, operator edits, recovery behavior, and future upgrade compatibility.

options.title: Approve complete ownership lifecycle
options.body: Accept global MCP ownership only with explicit consent, create-only writes, deterministic pending reconciliation, compare-before-remove, and documented recovery semantics.

options.title: Defer MCP ownership
options.body: Keep MCP declarations unsupported until the RFC defines and proves a complete ownership and recovery boundary.

options.title: Make MCP advisory
options.body: Permit packages to describe MCP servers for export or setup guidance without mutating global configuration.

recommendation.title: Approve complete ownership lifecycle
recommendation.body: Accept global MCP ownership only with explicit consent, create-only writes, deterministic pending reconciliation, compare-before-remove, and documented recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses core product, executable configuration, persistent state, and RFC acceptance boundaries.
